Daily actual evapotranspiration

Source: R/metric-et.R
ef_et_daily.Rd

Extrapolates the instantaneous estimate at the satellite overpass time to the daily actual evapotranspiration \(ETa_{24}\) of the image day.

ef_et_daily() is the dispatcher of the family: it checks method and forwards the arguments to the function of that method, without any computation of its own. The methods are:

  • "etrf": ef_et_daily_etrf(), the reference evapotranspiration fraction (ETrF) of the overpass time multiplied by the daily reference evapotranspiration (METRIC).

Only "etrf" is implemented. The extrapolation by the evaporative fraction (a future ef_et_daily_evapfrac()) and the accumulation over a period between images (a future ef_et_period()) are not available yet: they need their own specification and verification.

Usage

ef_et_daily(etrf, etr_24, reference, method)

ef_et_daily_etrf(etrf, etr_24, reference)

Arguments

etrf

Numeric. Reference evapotranspiration fraction \(ETrF\) at the overpass time [-], from ef_etrf(). Any finite value; negative values are allowed and kept.

etr_24

Numeric. Reference evapotranspiration accumulated over the image day \(ETr_{24}\) [mm d-1]. Must be finite and >= 0.

reference

Character. The reference crop of etr_24, with no default: "alfalfa" (tall reference, ETr) or "grass" (short reference, ETo). It must be the reference used to compute etrf.

method

Character. The extrapolation method, with no default (the choice is a scientific decision that must be explicit). Currently only "etrf".

Value

A numeric vector of daily actual evapotranspiration \(ETa_{24}\) [mm d-1] with the common length of the inputs. If the inputs include matrices or arrays (all with the same dim), the result keeps that dim. Negative values are returned unchanged. ef_et_daily() returns exactly the value of the method function.

Details

Method "etrf" computes $$ETa_{24} = ETrF \cdot ETr_{24}$$ where \(ETrF\) is etrf and \(ETr_{24}\) is etr_24, the cumulative reference evapotranspiration of the image day.

Assumption: the fraction \(ETrF\) at the overpass time is constant during the whole day, i.e. the actual evapotranspiration changes in proportion to the reference evapotranspiration. The assumption is weakened by the diurnal variation of the ratio (stomatal closure, drying of the soil surface after irrigation, increasing water stress), by the overpass time, by clouds after the overpass, by the night hours included in \(ETr_{24}\), by terrain (no slope correction is applied) and by mixed pixels at about 1 km. A common multiplicative bias of the instantaneous and daily reference evapotranspiration cancels: the result depends on the ratio \(ETr_{24} / ETr_{inst}\).

Reference crop: etrf and etr_24 must refer to the same reference crop (and to the same one as the cold anchor pixel). reference does not change the computation: it makes the choice explicit. The consistency check between the steps is made by the orchestration layer.

Slope correction: the correction of the daily energy availability in sloping terrain used by some METRIC implementations is not applied; its form and source are pending verification.

Negative values of etrf give a negative daily evapotranspiration, returned unchanged and without a warning (never set to zero). With etr_24 = 0 the result is zero whatever the sign of etrf. The diagnostic flag EF_ET_NEGATIVE is assembled by the orchestration layer on this layer.

Missing values (NA, NaN) in any input propagate to the corresponding output element, without errors or warnings. Arguments must be numeric (double or integer) and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled, arrays with a dim are not. A negative etr_24 or any infinite value raises an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). A missing method, reference or method argument raises earthflux_missing_input; an unknown method, earthflux_unknown_method; an unknown reference, earthflux_input_error.

Verification status: method "etrf" is CANDIDATA (corroborated by secondary sources, Olmedo et al., 2016, Eq. 4). It is implemented as an operational definition; its form and equation number in Allen et al. (2007) have not been verified.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Olmedo, G. F., Ortega-Farias, S., de la Fuente-Saiz, D., Fonseca-Luengo, D., & Fuentes-Penailillo, F. (2016). water: Tools and functions to estimate actual evapotranspiration using land surface energy balance models in R. The R Journal, 8(2), 352-369. doi:10.32614/RJ-2016-051

See also

Other latent heat and evapotranspiration functions: ef_et_inst(), ef_etrf(), ef_latent_heat()

Examples

# ETrF 0.9 and 8 mm d-1 of alfalfa reference ET: 7.2 mm d-1
ef_et_daily(etrf = 0.9, etr_24 = 8, reference = "alfalfa",
            method = "etrf")
#> [1] 7.2

# Same result calling the method directly
ef_et_daily_etrf(etrf = 0.9, etr_24 = 8, reference = "alfalfa")
#> [1] 7.2

# Full chain from the energy balance (one pixel)
lambda <- ef_lambda(method = "constant")
le <- ef_latent_heat(rn = 600, g = 60, h = 50)
et_inst <- ef_et_inst(le, lambda)
etrf <- ef_etrf(et_inst, etr_inst = 0.80, reference = "alfalfa")
ef_et_daily(etrf, etr_24 = 8, reference = "alfalfa", method = "etrf")
#> [1] 7.2
